name: זְבוּלֻן
summary: Jacob’s tenth son, the sixth born to him by Leah, and the tribe that came from him, which camped east of the tabernacle in Judah’s camp and set out with it, first on the march, under Eliab son of Helon (Num 2:7; 10:16); Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel (Jdg 12:11). Leah named him with the verb of the root: “this time my husband will זָבַל me”, honour her or dwell with her (Gen 30:20), and the root’s noun זְבֻל is a lofty dwelling (1Ki 8:13). Jacob’s blessing has him dwell (יִשְׁכֹּן) at the shore of the seas (Gen 49:13). Isaiah’s “land of Zebulun” that sees a great light is fulfilled, Matthew says, when Jesus comes to live at Capernaum in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali (Isa 8:23–9:1; Mat 4:13–16).

evidence.note: “This time my husband will זָבַל me (יִזְבְּלֵנִי), for I have borne him six sons; and she called his name זְבֻלוּן.”
The root’s noun: “a בֵּית זְבֻל for you, a place for your dwelling for ever”.
“Zebulun shall dwell at the shore of the seas, and he shall be a shore for ships, and his side toward Sidon.”
Moses: “Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out … they shall suck the abundance of the seas.”
For Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon.
Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon, setting out in the camp of Judah.
“Zebulun was a people that risked their lives to the death.”
From Zebulun, those who handle the scribe’s staff.
Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel ten years.
“He brought contempt on the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but afterward he has made glorious the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.”
Jesus lives at Capernaum “in the borders of Ζαβουλών and Naphtali”, fulfilling Isaiah’s word.
One of the city’s south gates, the gate of Zebulun.
Of the tribe of Zebulun twelve thousand were sealed.

note: Takes g.af.ad (the name, 45 tokens) and the gentilic זְבוּלֹנִי (g.af.ae, 3 tokens), which TIPNR lists as a form of Zebulun@Gen.30.20. g.af.ad also counts the tribe’s land (Jos 19:27; Isa 8:23). The text spells it זְבֻלוּן and זְבוּלֻן; the Septuagint and New Testament Ζαβουλών. Whether Leah’s verb means “honour” or “dwell with” is open (see the root entry).
